narrative: Material PL1__M61C6B28 exhibits smooth, normally-distributed daily demand averaging 479 units with a CV of 0.30, indicating stable and predictable consumption patterns. Lead times average 4.1 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.37), and 3 erroneous lead-time records (including a 9327-day anomaly) were removed prior to analysis. The recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy raises safety stock from 152 to 1,300 units — necessary to achieve the 95% service level given the combined demand-lead time sigma of 790 units. The storage cap of 3,144 units constrains the order quantity below the theoretical EOQ optimum, slightly increasing annual costs.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ=3337 capped to OQ=1844 (max_storage_units=3144, safety_stock=1300)
SAP safety stock (152) is critically below recommended level (1300) — high stockout risk under current ERP parameters
3 lead-time records removed as data errors: values 9327.37, 0.03, 0.01 days

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, high-frequency demand with 100% non-zero days and moderate lead-time variability makes continuous review optimal. The (r,Q) model minimises total cost by triggering a fixed replenishment order Q whenever on-hand inventory hits reorder point r, providing tight control without excess safety stock inflation.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap (3,144 units) prevents achieving the unconstrained EOQ of 3,337 units, forcing a smaller order of 1,844 units. This increases ordering frequency from ~37 to ~68 orders/year, raising annual ordering costs by approximately 84% vs. unconstrained optimum. If storage capacity can be expanded, reverting to EOQ would reduce total annual cost.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (168) + safety_stock (1300) = 1468 units, which is below max_storage_units (3144). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
